purpose: Matured, post-backfill re-take of docs/paphos-offplan-baseline-2026-08-27.json. That snapshot's absolute numbers are understated by roughly an order of magnitude -- captured before SearchMetric's one-time 90-day backfill (see docs/de-villa-cluster-baseline-2026-09-01.json's ingestCaveat for the mechanism: every historical row was originally captured once, 2 days after its date, under a too-narrow re-fetch window that caught GSC data before it had matured, and never revisited). Comparing matured data against that unrevised baseline would read as growth that did not happen. This file is the comparable 'after' point.
caveat: Even matured GSC data keeps revising for roughly a month after each date, and ordinary day-to-day/week-to-week drift is real on this cluster independent of any site change (documented repeatedly across this investigation). This window (28 days, see below) does not calendar-overlap the original's window at all -- it is a fresh 28-day lookback from today, not a continuation -- so a direct number-for-number diff against the original is not meaningful; use this as the new reference point going forward, not as a delta calculation against the 08-27 file.

notComparableTo.reason: pre-backfill, absolute numbers understated -- see that file's own header note (added 2026-09-09) before using it for any comparison.

whatChangedSincePriorSnapshot.summary: Two independent things changed on this page since 2026-08-27, both directly relevant to reading any future GSC movement here: (1) server-side pagination went fully live and discoverable only as of today; (2) for most of the time since the original snapshot, the page silently had LESS effective content surface than either the pre-pagination or the fully-fixed state.

paginationTimeline.event: Server-side pagination (pagesEnabled) built and deployed, opt-in, inert by default. commit 512feeb.

pagesEnabled verified live on this exact page with a real, server-rendered pager (real <a href="?page=N"> links) -- this is the day this baseline snapshot itself was captured. The page was, as of this date, both paginated AND discoverable via its own on-page pager.

An unrelated visual redesign rebuilt the landing-page component tree from scratch and did not port pagination's pager markup over -- not deliberate, simply missing from that redesign's parity checklist. From this date, ?page=2+ was still server-correct (200, right content, right canonical) but had ZERO discovery path: no pager link anywhere on the page, and the sitemap never had ?page= entries for this page at any point since pagination was introduced (a separate, then-accepted backlog decision, not a regression -- see below).
Pager markup restored (PR #23) and page 2+ added to the sitemap for the first time ever on this page (same PR). Both landed and were deployed together.

whatChangedSincePriorSnapshot.correctedFigure: The instruction that prompted this file described the pager as 'missing for 13 days.' The precise pager-missing window, by commit timestamps, is 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-09 -- 7 days, not 13. Thirteen days IS the correct span from this baseline's own capture date (2026-08-27) to today (2026-09-09) -- but for 6 of those 13 days (08-27 to 09-02) the pager was live and working; it was missing for the remaining 7. Separately, and worth keeping distinct from the pager question: sitemap ?page= entries did not exist for this page on ANY day across the full 13-day span -- that gap was a deliberate, documented backlog decision on 08-27 ("pager links alone will carry discovery"), not a bug, until today's fix. See docs/SITE-CHANGELOG.md, 2026-09-09 entries, for the full incident writeup.
whatChangedSincePriorSnapshot.readingCaution: Any GSC position/impression movement on this page across 2026-08-27 to 2026-09-09 happened while the page had NO functioning discovery path to page 2+ content for the great majority of that window (7 of 13 days with zero pager, all 13 days with zero sitemap entries). Movement in this window should not be read as evidence pagination helped or hurt visibility -- the mechanism was not actually reachable by a crawler for nearly the entire period being measured.

window.note: Open-ended 28-day lookback window from capture, same convention as the original file. Freshest SearchMetric data for this page as of capture: 2026-09-06 (normal ~3-day GSC reporting lag -- inherent to GSC itself, unrelated to the ingestion-window bug the backfill fixed).
